description.narrative: The UK Government, through FCDO, will provide multi‑year core funding from 2026–2029 to the British Red Cross (BRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), supporting their wide‑ranging humanitarian mandates across crisis preparedness, response, protection, and system‑strengthening within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Under a joint BRC–IFRC–ICRC Business Case, FCDO will contribute up to £4.5 million directly to BRC as flexible core funding, with 30% of disbursements linked to performance against an agreed logframe. In addition, under the Joint Business Case for 2026–2029, BRC will receive, on behalf of the IFRC, a total allocation of £16.5 million (£5.5 million per year over three years). As set out in a tripartite Memorandum of Understanding between FCDO, BRC, and IFRC, BRC will act as the intermediary for these IFRC funds and will transfer them directly to the IFRC Secretariat upon receipt. BRC will continue to work in close partnership with FCDO, IFRC and the wider Movement to address today’s most urgent humanitarian challenges. This includes accelerating preparedness and anticipatory action, supporting principled humanitarian access, strengthening National Society capacities, advancing protection and international legal norms, and ensuring accountable, inclusive and effective services for crisis‑affected people.

This grant is for the direct transfer of £1.1M received from FCDO [Second tranche of unearmarked Funds non-Payment by Result (PBR) funding from the total £5.5M], to the IFRC for their Core Funding allocation under the joint IFRC-BRC Business Case 2026-2030 for the year 2026.

This grant is for the direct transfer of £2.75M received from FCDO [First tranche of unearmarked Funds non-Payment by Result (PBR) funding from the total £5.5M], to the IFRC for their Core Funding allocation under the joint IFRC-BRC Business Case 2026-2030 (with one year extension) for the year 2026.
